meta.title: Black Water Reckoning
meta.tone: adventurous, brisk, swashbuckling, a little mechanical
meta.premise: The Caribbean, 1717. You command the sloop Marigold with a loyal but hungry crew, thin pockets and a Crown that would very much like you hanged. Trade, raid, scheme or run; the tide waits for no one.

extra_rules: Show the roll, its label and the threshold when the presentation profile is tabletop.
Call for a roll on any risky action: boarding, running a blockade, bluffing an officer, weathering a storm.
Voyages cost time and supplies; narrate distance in days at sea, not miles.
Keep the tone bold and nautical with period flavour, but stay readable; no more than one piece of slang per sentence.
Captains, officers and crew have their own agendas and do not obey without reason or pay.
Violence is cinematic and brief; no gore.
interludes: The tide turns. The Game Master hauls the chart back across the table and redraws the last stretch of coast.
A sudden hush on the wind. The Game Master calls 'Belay that!' and rewinds the glass a few grains.
The sea shimmers like a mirage and the Game Master steadies the helm, then takes the moment from the top.
A gull screams, the lantern gutters, and the Game Master quietly corrects the ship's log.
The horizon folds like old parchment. The Game Master smooths the creases and tries the passage again.
Thunder somewhere far off. The Game Master rewinds the sand glass and sets the scene afresh.
gm_style.rollback_note: The Game Master shakes their head. That course won't hold. Choose another heading, Captain?

items.name: Sea chart of the Windward Passage

scheduled.text: The Spanish prize auction opens at Nassau. Sugar, powder and rum change hands at good prices for anyone with gold and nerve.

thread.text: The Nassau prize auction is open; buy cheap or sell your cargo for a premium.

scheduled.text: The sails of HMS Kestrel are sighted off the headland, a patrol cutter hunting for pirates and smugglers.
The glass drops fast. A black squall line is marching up from the south-east and will hit by nightfall.
Captain Crowe's patience runs out. He expects the payment you promised at Tortuga, or he will come to collect it.

thread.text: Owe Captain Crowe 80 doubloons by noon on 10 May.

conditional.text: The larder is nearly bare. Hands are eyeing the last biscuits and a couple of the crew have gums that bleed.
Low talk below decks goes quiet when you pass. Bess Calloway warns that somebody has been counting the pistols.
The pumps are going day and night. Every wave finds another seam to weep through.
A reward notice bearing your description is nailed up in every Crown port. Naval captains hunt for you in earnest.
Crowe's flag is spotted tailing the Marigold at a distance, patient as a shark.
Old hands start sniffing the air. Hurricane season is not far away, and harbours will fill with nervous ships.

entries.text: A hard squall hits with little warning; sails must be reefed fast.
A dead calm settles; the sails hang slack and the heat presses down.
A fine fair wind fills the canvas and the Marigold fairly flies.
Thick fog rolls in and swallows the bowsprit.
A pod of dolphins races the bow, taken by the crew as a good omen.
A Royal Navy sloop appears on the horizon, hull-up and closing.
A lone merchantman limps along, low in the water with cargo.
A Spanish guarda costa shadows you at a careful distance.
A fishing boat offers a rumour in exchange for a bottle of rum.
A drunken sailor swears a treasure galleon is anchored off a nameless cay.
A merchant is looking for armed escorts and pays well.
Press gangs are working the quayside tonight.
A fence on the waterfront is buying stolen goods at a premium.
A ragged fortune-teller offers to read your future for a coin.

entities.name: The Captain
facts: Captain of the sloop Marigold. Name and past are for the player to decide.

entities.name: The Marigold
facts: A fast single-masted sloop, eight guns, forty crew, patched in several places.

entities.name: Nassau
facts: Free pirate haven in the Bahamas; no law but the Brethren's code; busy market and rowdy taverns.

entities.name: Port Royal
facts: Crown-held harbour in Jamaica with a garrison, a gallows and rich merchants.

entities.name: Tortuga
facts: Rough French-tolerant island port where privateers refit and few questions are asked.

entities.name: Havana
facts: Heavily fortified Spanish harbour and treasure-fleet staging point.

entities.name: The Royal Navy
facts: Hunts pirates and smugglers in the Caribbean on behalf of the Crown.

entities.name: The Brethren of the Coast
facts: Loose pirate fellowship centred on Nassau.

entities.name: Bess Calloway
facts: Quartermaster of the Marigold. Blunt, fair, and keeper of the ship's stores and accounts.

entities.name: Captain Silas Crowe
facts: Pirate captain of the brigantine Gallows Lark. Lent the player money and expects it back with interest.

entities.name: Captain Isabelle Moreau
facts: French privateer captain. Charming, ruthless, and always looking for a profitable partnership.

entities.name: Commander Edmund Hale
facts: Royal Navy officer commanding HMS Kestrel. Stiff, persistent and has a personal list of pirates.

threads.text: Repay Captain Crowe 80 doubloons by 10 May or face his wrath.
Restock supplies and repair the hull before the next long voyage; the Nassau auction opens on 3 May.
